text: Alright, so today we're setting up this advanced 3-axis CNC router that was installed by our team last week in the main workshop. First, I need to hook up the precision spindle motor that can reach speeds of up to 24,000 RPM. The high-quality carbide end mill with a 6-millimeter diameter, which Sarah recommended from the premium tooling catalog, gets loaded into the collet. Now, while I'm putting together the workholding fixtures, the machine bed was already calibrated by the morning shift technician using a dial indicator. Next, I'll turn on the vacuum system and fire up the spindle motor. The MDF workpiece that we're cutting today measures exactly 300 by 200 millimeters and is 18 millimeters thick. After that, the cutting parameters were programmed by our CNC operator - we're running at 1500 millimeters per minute feed rate with a 2-millimeter depth of cut. The experienced machinist with over 15 years of CNC experience starts the program while monitoring the cutting forces. Then, as the router cuts through the material, wood chips and dust get sucked up by the industrial vacuum system. The final part dimensions are checked by Sarah using precision calipers, and the surface finish that was achieved measures less than 32 microinches roughness. Before we wrap up, I need to clean up the workspace and shut down the coolant system.
